top_problem: The idea is not ownable. An engraved agave rising from the lower right of a near-black page with a spaced serif CANTINA is almost exactly ref-02 panel 1, and the 'Iowa soil' that is meant to carry the Mexico and Iowa fusion (Brief §5) reads as scattered confetti or ash rather than prairie loam. Without the proposal text no guest would see Iowa, so the design fails the substitution test. The boldest idea it is missing is Iowa made visible in the drawing: agave grown from ploughed Iowa furrows or contour rows, a corn and agave hybrid of the same engraved hand, or the rosette sitting on a real Johnson County section-grid horizon, drawn in one grammar with the leaves.
remove: The 650 crumb strokes and the two broken strata lines in the loam band. Their random tick grammar differs from the tapered engraved leaves, they are the brightest-density area at the bottom edge and they pull the eye off the list. Replace them with engraved furrow hatching in the leaf grammar, or leave the loam as quiet plate tone.
fixes: Redraw the soil as Iowa ploughed furrows or contour rows in the same tapered engraved line as the leaves, with lower density and lower contrast than the rosette, so the fusion is readable without a caption and the band stops competing as a sixth focal region.

Close the 14.8 mm column-end gap (784 vs 728) by rebalancing Wine or Cider into col 2 or moving Spirits' Brandy block, and fill or deliberately shape the empty field under Cognac VSOP at bottom left instead of leaving canvas.

Add a second, warm Mexican ink (terracotta or marigold used on prices or one art accent at <=3%) so the palette stops reading as a monochrome sage on black; ref-02 panels 1 and 5 show how one warm accent lifts this ground.

Make the wordmark ownable: give CANTINA a custom treatment tied to the thesis (for example, the soil line running through the baseline, or an engraved inline) rather than the stock wide-tracked serif that ref-02 already shows twice.
Snap the phone rows back to the 8 px baseline (mod8 currently 3, 7 and 1) and raise the 11 px tracked sub-labels to 12 px for dim-bar legibility.

lens: items and prices against build/draft_doc.json; ingredient names and how complete descriptions are (meta.public_components); section flow for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: Every item and price is correct. The cocktails are fully described, but the other 9 items (beer, cider, wine, spirits) carry thin placeholder lines copied from the draft. The three spirits lines just repeat the item name ('Blanco tequila pour' under Blanco Tequila), so more than half the menu reads like a stock list. On top of that, the reading path runs Cocktails > Spirits and then jumps up to Beer > Cider > Wine, and a large drawing that competes for attention sits beside column 2.
problems: All 15 items and all 15 prices match the draft exactly: Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18. Nothing is invented or dropped.

Hidden components are handled correctly: meta.public_components sets aromatic-bitters to false for the Manhattan, and the printed line leaves the bitters out. The Old Fashioned's aromatic bitters are public and are printed.

The four garnishes (lime wheel, cocktail cherry, lime coin, orange peel) are cited to phg.recipe_versions f06abb74, 9fb77eaa, 14d45e57 and 7095fd3d. I could not check those rows in this fast pass; the accuracy reviewer should confirm them.
The Classics order was changed from the draft (Manhattan first) to Margarita first, and proposal.md does not note it. The change suits a Mexican venue, but it is undocumented.

Known data gap (Rob to supply, not the designer's fault): no beer ABV, no wine region, no spirit brand or producer. As a result beer, wine and spirits fail the criterion 8 standard (beer style + ABV, wine grape + region, spirit type/age + brand). The agave list has no mezcal and no reposado, which is thin for a cantina.

The three spirits descriptions ('Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour') are draft wording that only repeats the item name. They add no information and fill the space where the missing data should go.

The voice is inconsistent: only the Margarita has an italic tasting note ('Bright and citrus-forward.', from the draft). The other three cocktails have none, so the Margarita reads as featured without a reason.
Brut Rosé 13 has no pour label (glass or bottle), and a Sparkling subhead now separates it from the 'By the Glass' subhead above. A guest cannot tell whether 13 is a glass price or a bottle price.

Flow: the draft order is Cocktails > Beer > Wine > Spirits > Cider. The design puts Spirits under Cocktails in column 1 and Beer > Cider > Wine in column 2. Leading with agave spirits is defensible for this venue, but a Z-read takes the guest from Cocktails to Spirits and then back up to Beer. The columns end at different heights (784 vs 728 px), and the large rosette to the right of the wine block pulls the eye away from the list (the render's own squint test counts 5 salient regions).
There is no non-alcoholic section. The draft has none, so this is not the designer's fault, but for this venue a cantina without aguas frescas or NA options is an obvious gap to raise with Rob.

Prices use one inline style (plain whole numbers, no $, about 5% eye travel, so no remote-price issue). But they are ragged: each price sits at a different x because it follows the length of its name. That makes price-to-price comparison harder within Spirits and Wine, and the prices are muted to nearly the weight of the names.

There are no taglines, section-rule taglines or prop captions. The '& Cocktail Bar / Iowa City, Iowa' sub-line states only venue facts, so no item fact appears in any tagline. 'CANTINA' is still a placeholder venue name.
fixes: Ask Rob to fill beer style/ABV, wine grape/region and spirit brand/age now. Until then, mark the gaps as missing_ingredients in the build rather than printing descriptions that just repeat the item name. For example, show only the item name for spirits, or print 'Blanco tequila · 100% agave' only if the source confirms it.
Add a 'glass' or 'bottle' label to Brut Rosé 13 once Rob confirms the pour. Otherwise move the 'By the Glass' label up to the Wine header so it clearly covers all three wines.
Either give every cocktail a one-line draft-sourced tasting note or drop the italic line from the Margarita. As printed, one cocktail looks featured without a stated reason.

Make the reading path explicit. Either run column 1 as Cocktails > Draft Beer > Cider and column 2 as Wine > Spirits, or keep agave spirits beside cocktails but pair them in one row band. Balance the column ends to within one 8 px step. Also note the Margarita-first reordering in proposal.md.
Flag the missing non-alcoholic/aguas frescas category and the mezcal/reposado gaps to Rob as venue-fit data requests. Do not add them to the design until the data exists.

lens: Ingredient/garnish/label traceability to build/draft_doc.json and phg.recipe_versions; how descriptions sit with prices in preview-letter.png; price-to-item gate
top_problem: Every printed fact on the menu is sourced, but it gives a guest little reason to order. Two of the three spirits descriptions just repeat the item name word for word ('Blanco Tequila' / 'Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo Tequila' / 'Añejo tequila pour'), and the third reorders it ('Cognac VSOP' / 'VSOP Cognac pour'). The beer and cider lines nearly do the same ('Amber Lager' / 'Toasty amber lager', 'Dry Cider' / 'Dry sparkling cider'). The wine lines are category labels ('Dry red wine'). Criterion 12 rejects all of these. The page also uses three voices: lowercase cocktail ingredient lists joined by middots, flat beer and wine fragments, and one italic tasting note on the Margarita only. And 'Tequila blanco' in the Margarita clashes with 'Blanco Tequila' three inches below. Verified sources: all 4 garnishes match phg.recipe_versions via the menu_items.current_recipe_version_id join: Margarita f06abb74 'Lime wheel' (Rocks), Manhattan 9fb77eaa 'Cocktail cherry' (Coupe), House Daiquiri 14d45e57 'Lime coin' (Coupe), Brown Butter Old Fashioned 7095fd3d 'Orange peel' (Rocks). Every printed ingredient traces to draft_doc.json components: Tequila Blanco, Fresh Lime Juice, Orange Liqueur, Agave Syrup; Rye Whiskey, Sweet Vermouth, with Aromatic Bitters correctly hidden (public_components 'aromatic-bitters': false); White Rum, Fresh Lime Juice, Demerara Syrup printed as 'house demerara syrup', backed by the draft desc; Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon, Demerara Syrup, Aromatic Bitters. 'Bright and citrus-forward.' comes from the Margarita desc. Every beer, cider, wine and spirits line is draft desc text word for word. All 14 prices sit inline, 30 px or less after their names, so association passes. No invented ABV, region, brand, grape or glass appears anywhere (these are the known gap). The wordmark 'CANTINA' is a placeholder, not an item fact.
fixes: Replace the name-echo spirits lines with sourced guest language once Rob supplies spirit_lexicon or brand rows (brand, agave origin, age statement), and until then drop the description rather than print 'Blanco tequila pour' under 'Blanco Tequila'.

Pick one voice for the whole page: either ingredient lists for every item (wine grape and region, beer style and ABV once Rob supplies them) or short sensory lines for every item, and drop the Margarita's italic note unless every cocktail gets one from a sourced desc.

Make the tequila wording consistent: use 'Blanco tequila' in the Margarita list to match the 'Blanco Tequila' spirits item (draft component 'Tequila Blanco'), or ask Rob which form is the house style, and print 'demerara syrup' the same way in the Daiquiri and the Old Fashioned (both are house-prep rows in the draft).

Venue fit: add sourced Spanish section kickers (for example 'Cócteles', 'Cerveza de barril', 'Vino') and ask Rob for a Mexican lager and a mezcal row, because a cantina whose draft list is Czech Pilsner, IPA and Amber Lager, with Cognac under Brandy, reads as a generic Iowa bar wearing an agave.

Layout note for the designer: the Daiquiri wraps after 'fresh lime juice ·', which leaves a short first line and puts middots at line ends on 2 of 4 cocktails. Rebalance the measure or let the bound pair break so the lines fill evenly, and give Brut Rosé and the by-the-glass wines a pour label once Rob supplies one.
